# Hutsix — Windows Automation Toolkit

Hutsix is a Windows automation toolkit with keyboard macros, OCR and image screen triggers, and AI-assisted calibration. Free 7-day trial for Windows 10/11.

## What Hutsix does

- Keyboard Macros — Map and fire keyboard actions from global hotkeys.
- OCR & Image Triggers — Detect on-screen text and visual patterns you define.
- AI Calibration — OpenCV + AI-assisted calibration keeps triggers accurate.
- Profiles — Switchable profiles with foreground-window detection.

Free 7-day trial. Full feature set during the trial. A paid license is required after it expires; the trial cannot be reset by reinstalling.

## How it works

Hutsix organizes automation into profiles made of bindings. Each binding pairs a trigger with an action: a trigger detects an event (global hotkey, pixel color, image match, or OCR text), and an action plays a keyboard or mouse sequence. When a profile is active, a watchdog engine continuously evaluates bindings and executes actions only when the configured conditions are satisfied.

1. Install a Hutsix release and launch the app.
2. Create or import a profile.
3. Add a trigger (hotkey, pixel, image, or OCR text).
4. Attach an action sequence (keyboard or mouse playback).
5. Activate the profile and validate behavior with the Action Monitor and per-binding diagnostics.

## Use cases

- Gaming: Auto-looting in MMOs, buff management and ability rotations, frame-perfect input sequences for fighting games.
- Productivity: Data-entry automation from screenshots, form filling with OCR detection, batch processing triggers.
- Content Creation: Frame capturing for streaming overlays, automated editing triggers during recording, screenshot batch processing.
- Developer Tools: UI testing automation and screenshot-based regression testing workflows.

## System requirements

- OS: Windows 10/11 (64-bit)
- CPU: 6+ logical cores
- RAM: 16 GB for core automation; 32 GB recommended for AI modules (YOLOX/OCR/training)
- GPU: NVIDIA with CUDA recommended for best YOLOX/OCR performance (8 GB+ VRAM preferred); CPU fallback supported
- Storage: SSD with 10 GB+ free space (more for datasets and models)

Hutsix supports both CPU and GPU execution paths. CUDA-enabled acceleration applies to supported AI and vision workloads, and features fall back to CPU when GPU acceleration is unavailable.

## Privacy

Hutsix is a local desktop application. Profiles, logs, and runtime data are stored locally on your system. Licensing checks may contact the licensing provider during activation or verification.

## FAQ

Q: Is Hutsix free?
A: Hutsix offers a free 7-day trial with the full feature set. A paid license is required after the trial expires.

Q: Does Hutsix work with Windows 11?
A: Yes — Hutsix supports Windows 10 and Windows 11, 64-bit.

Q: Can the Hutsix trial be reset by reinstalling?
A: No. The trial is anchored on your machine and cannot be reset by reinstalling the app.

Q: Is coding required to use Hutsix?
A: No. Typical usage is fully UI-driven; no custom scripts are needed.

Q: Can I share my profiles?
A: Yes. Profiles are reusable and shareable through import and export.

Q: Does Hutsix inject into game memory?
A: No. Hutsix is designed around input simulation and screen/foreground detection.

Q: Does Hutsix support GPU acceleration?
A: Yes. CUDA-enabled acceleration is available for supported AI and vision workloads, with automatic CPU fallback when a GPU is unavailable.

Q: Can automation violate third-party terms?
A: Yes. Some apps and services prohibit automation. Users are responsible for how they use the software.
